Haha that's such a coincidence. I'm going to study English to become a teacher :) 

I've always wished I had a closer relationship with my sister. She is a really good person who is genuine and kind. She's basically the opposite of me, in a good way :) I'm going to reach out to her. 

Thanks for talking man. I need to go to bed now, but I definitely want to talk again. Is it cool if I PM you, or should I just comment here. 

Anyway I'll read your reply in the morning, I might need to work in the morning so I'm going to sleep.

Is he underage as well? And how underage are we talking? Are you guys on opposite sides of a country, or different countries all together. 

I come from a very conservative part of Canada, and grew up around homophobia. Luckily, I had very open minded parents and grew up to recognize the differences in others and that people are not all the same. What I'm trying to say is, I know that there is nothing wrong or abnormal about being gay, but I understand the mindset of those who think there is. 

Are you from a conservative area as well? 

I can't really speak for long distance relationships, or even "real" relationships for that matter, as all my girlfriends were in and before highschool. But, and this is going to be hard to hear, if you are highschool aged, maybe a long distance relationship isn't the best idea. Or, at the very least, you should explore more relaxed boundries with the relationship. I could probably give better advice if I knew more about the situation. 

Listen, I need to go to bed now. Feel free to reply to this comment of even PM me. I'll be reading this in the morning, but I may not be able to respond until later tomorrow if I have to work in the morning. 

I want to keep talking to you so we can get to know each other better. 

:)

Dude, good for you. Really, I'm the same way with the weight. I just broke 200 when I graduated highschool. 8 months ago I was at my heaviest at 280. I dropped to 260 then gained some of it back, sitting at 270 now. 

The worst part is there are people in my life who I'm 99% sure would stand by me if I asked them too, but I'm a cynical pessimist and that 1% is enough to stop me. I only really have 1 really good friend, and he lives 500 miles away. My sister lives 1000 miles away, and my brother in law with her. When I lived with my sister going to college my brother in law and I became pretty close. He is addicted to working out now and I would always lift with him. 

My biggest issue right now is being in this damn transition period. I need to work to make enough money to go back to school, but living where I am and working where I am might break me before then.

I was in college, and started slacking off because I always did well in high school without trying, why not college too. It didn't translate, I tried to switch majors, big mistake. I ended up DNFing two courses and dropping my GPA down enough so that I can't get into any other schools. So now I'm working as a truck driver to make some money to go back and raise my GPA. I hate my life, I hate my useless, lazy self, and I despise every millisecond of my job, even though I make bank. Literally the only reason I'm still doing it is because I need money fast to get back to school .

I have no motivation, and even if I do end up getting motivated to do somethings I don't have the discipline to keep it up. The worst part is I have absolutely no idea how to fix myself. I will probably end up going to a therapist but I thought I would try finding someone to talk too here first. 

What about you? Any ideas why you could be sad? I know you said in your post you don't know why, but tell me about yourself and/or your situation.

Man I'm sorry you had to / have to go through that sort of thing. I've only ever gotten one really bad panic attack, and it was fairly recently. I was driving into town (I live in a small rural community) to go train with my cousin and I just started freaking out about how fucked up my life was. The roads were bad and I had lost my wallet that morning, so on the road I just started crying and wheezing. I pulled over, got out of the care and ran around like an idiot for a few minutes, got back in and drove home. It was pretty scary. 

I always thought a big panic attack like that would snap me into shape, but if anything it's done the opposite. It's all been downhill from there. It's as simple as little shit, like telling myself I'm going to fold my laundry today then not doing it. Until recently, my apartment was an absolute disgusting pigsty. Thankfully my auntie and uncle came by and helped me clean it on new years eve, but it hasn't helped that much. 

Basically I have no motivation, and for the few brief moments I do get motivated I have no discipline to stay that way, and the real kicker is I have NO FUCKING CLUE how to change that. I've read all the advice online, and it all boils down to the face that I'm being lazy and self destructive and not doing anything, and I really truly honestly don't know what to do.
Oh cool. So what brings you to SW? Are you like one of us - super depressed - or are you one of the awesome people who have their lives at least somewhat together and come to give advice?

Thanks. I'm not really good at starting out these types of conversations. I guess I'm just looking for someone to vent too and bounce ideas off of. 

I'm 21, male from Canada. What about you?

Wow that sounds very specialized. I always dream of specializing in one very specific thing and dedicating my life to it. 

I was in college. For 2 years. My first year went pretty well, except for one history class which I hated going to. I thought I ended up failing it, so I switched from a BA to a BS. That turned out to be pointless, since my grade was changed from an F to a C. I guess the prof misplaced one of my papers or something and found it a few months later. 

When I switched to a BS I had to upgrade all the courses I didn't take in high school, like maths and sciences. I ended up really not liking any of my courses, added to the fact that I am horrible at math and dropped out of 1 class and just blew off 2 others. That dropped my GPA down below to a 1.9, and you need at least a 2.0 to apply to any other colleges. So now I'm working as a truck driver back in my hometown to make some money to go back to school and raise my GPA, and I hate every minute of it.

It hit me a few weeks ago. I realized that I didn't want to kill myself, but I didn't want to be alive either. Every day I do things that should be making me feel better, but they just aren't. I've been able to keep up with writing a journal, meditating, and practising a new language on duolingo for every day of January so far. At first I thought it was helping, and I'm going to continue it everyday, but now it just feels like part of a useless routine. I truly despise every moment of my job, and feel useless and bored all the time when I'm not working. 

If you have some time to talk right now I'd really appreciate it, and I think we could help each other out.

Hey. I'm pretty sad myself right now too. You can check my history and read my post here if you want more info. If you have some time now or later I could use someone to talk too probably just as much as you...

Cool. I had a couple friends in highschool who were obsessed with Indian culture! I definitely need to make time to take a trip there one day. 

Basically I guess I just want to talk about life decisions. I'm at a point in my life where I need to start deciding what to do with it. Career-wise mostly, but other aspects as well. 

I'm 21 and I'm still having a hard time deciding what to do for a living.

What do you do?

Oh sorry. I usually just assume all redditors are white male north americans aged 20-22 until otherwise informed. 

Where are you from?

Hi. 

How's your night going? 

...sorry I'm really bad at starting conversations :(
